name: Telecom CDR fraud — wholesale / IRSF / bypass
parent_research_topic: Beava use cases — current and potential applications of beava as a real-time feature server

domain_fit.domain_name: Telecom wholesale-fraud detection from Call Detail Records (CDRs): IRSF (International Revenue Share Fraud), SIM-box / bypass fraud, Wangiri / flash-call abuse, A2P SMS pumping / AIT (Artificially Inflated Traffic), subscription fraud and PBX-hacking.
domain_fit.one_line_definition: A telco / wholesale-voice carrier / CPaaS fraud-ops engineer must decide within seconds (and ideally within milliseconds at the SBC / SMSC) whether to allow, throttle, or block an in-flight call leg or SMS based on per-A-number / per-B-number / per-destination-prefix / per-route streaming velocity and behavioural features computed from the CDR / EDR stream.
domain_fit.representative_jobs_to_be_done: Three concrete jobs: (1) Detect IRSF in-flight by computing per-A-number and per-(A,B-prefix) velocities (calls, minutes, distinct B-numbers, time-of-day skew, country-of-destination novelty) against the GLF / i3Forum / IPRN test-number hot lists and short-circuit at the SBC before the call completes its first billed minute — the published NDSS-2021 result is 98% accuracy / 0.28% FPR using exactly this feature class. (2) Spot SIM-box / bypass fraud signatures from CDR-only side-channel features: very high outbound-to-inbound call ratio per A-number, near-zero incoming-call diversity, abnormally flat call-duration distribution, repeated cell-tower set, low ratio of on-net to off-net, no SMS / no data, calls clustered to the same B-country — see Subex / Neural Technologies / Ethio-Telecom case studies citing ~99% recall within 10 minutes of usage. (3) Block A2P SMS pumping / AIT in real time on the CPaaS path by aggregating per-MSISDN, per-destination-MCCMNC, per-application, per-sender-ID counters and rate-of-change distributions (sequential-number ratio, conversion-rate collapse, geographic anomaly), then deciding inside the OTP-send budget (Twilio, Sinch, Bandwidth, Vonage, Plivo, Infobip explicitly publish this control). Sub-jobs include Wangiri / flash-call detection (zero/short-duration outbound bursts to broad MSISDN ranges, prompting call-backs to premium numbers) and subscription-fraud onboarding scoring (per-new-subscriber 1m/1h/24h velocity to high-cost destinations).
domain_fit.event_shapes: Typical events that would land in beava as @bv.event records: voice_cdr {ts_start, ts_end, duration_s, a_number_hash, b_number_hash, b_country, b_prefix, a_imsi_hash, a_imei_hash, cell_id, lac, rat (2G/3G/4G/5G/VoLTE/VoWiFi), call_type (mo/mt/forwarded/conf), trunk_id, peer_carrier, on_net, sip_response_code, billed_minutes, currency, charge_amount}; sms_edr {ts, a_number_hash, b_number_hash, b_country, b_mccmnc, sender_id, app_id, route_type (P2P/A2P), msg_class, parts, charge_amount, delivery_status}; signalling_event {ts, imsi_hash, imei_hash, msisdn_hash, event_type (location_update, attach, detach, supplementary_service_invoke, ussd, ss7_map_*), vlr_id, prev_vlr_id, source_country}; data_session_summary {ts, imsi_hash, apn, bytes_up, bytes_dn, duration_s, ggsn_id}; subscription_change {ts, msisdn_hash, account_id, plan_change, kyc_status_change, sim_swap_event, port_in/port_out}; verify_request / otp_send for CPaaS path {ts, app_id, dest_mccmnc, dest_country, dest_prefix, ip_hash, ua_hash, msisdn_hash, status}. Key fields are deliberately hashed (MSISDN, IMSI, IMEI) so beava state contains pseudonyms only and the box stays out of GDPR / ePrivacy CDR-retention scope wherever possible.
domain_fit.feature_shapes: Per-entity aggregations expressed as @bv.table primitives. Examples by entity: a_number_hash → count(calls, 1m/5m/1h/24h sliding), sum(billed_minutes, 1m/5m/1h/24h), n_unique(b_country, 1h/24h), n_unique(b_prefix, 1h/24h), distribution(duration_s, 1h) for SIM-box flat-distribution signature, ratio(outbound, inbound, 1h), share-to-high-risk-country distribution, time-since-first-call (subscription fraud aging), velocity of supplementary-service-invoke (call-forwarding abuse); b_number_hash → count(distinct a_number_hash, 1m/1h) for Wangiri fan-in, count(calls, 1m), distribution(duration_s, 1h) for zero-duration ratio; b_prefix (E.164 country / area / number-range) → count(calls, 1m/5m/1h), sum(billed_minutes, 1m), n_unique(a_number_hash, 1h), match-against-GLF / i3Forum / IPRN hot list, rate-of-change of attempts; (a_number_hash, b_country) pair → count, time-since-first-seen, never-before-called flag; cell_id / lac → n_unique(imsi_hash, 1h) for SIM-box co-located IMSIs, distribution(call_duration, 1h); imei_hash → n_unique(imsi_hash, 24h/7d) for IMEI-hopping; trunk_id / peer_carrier → count(calls to premium prefix, 1m), share-of-revenue-share-numbers distribution; (app_id, dest_country) for SMS pumping → count(otp_send, 1m/1h), sequential-MSISDN ratio, conversion-rate (delivered / engaged), per-MCCMNC fan-out (HLL n_unique). Mixed exact (counters / sums for billing-grade interconnect accounting) and approximate (HLL for distinct-B-number fan-out, CMS for top-K offending prefixes, t-digest for duration distributions).
domain_fit.entity_grain: Many parallel grains. Primary keys: a_number_hash (MSISDN), b_number_hash, b_prefix (E.164 country / area), imsi_hash, imei_hash, cell_id / lac (cell-tower), trunk_id, peer_carrier, app_id, sender_id, (a_number_hash, b_country) pair, (a_number_hash, b_prefix) pair, (app_id, dest_mccmnc) pair, route_id. A single decision typically reads features from 6–10 of these grains simultaneously.
domain_fit.window_semantics_required: All three plus session, with strong emphasis on sliding. Sliding windows dominate (10s, 1m, 5m, 15m, 1h, 24h, 7d) because IRSF / AIT bursts complete in seconds-to-minutes; tumbling windows show up for billing reconciliation (per-hour, per-day interconnect counts for carrier-to-carrier dispute resolution); session windows show up for SIM-box behaviour profiling (per-IMSI active session). Exact counts and sums are required for billing-grade interconnect accounting (carriers settle in real currency on these numbers). Approximate (HLL / CMS / t-digest) is acceptable and often preferred for high-cardinality B-number fan-out, distinct-MSISDN-per-app, and duration distributions feeding ML scorers — 1–2% HLL error is invisible against base rates.
domain_fit.exactly_once_or_idempotency_needs: Mixed. The fraud-blocking decision path tolerates at-least-once with idempotent counters (key = call_id / sms_id / cdr_id), because a duplicate count of one CDR does not change the threshold decision materially. However, interconnect-settlement counters (carrier-to-carrier billing reconciliation, GLF / i3Forum Code-of-Conduct attestation, regulator-facing fraud-loss accounting) require strict no-double-count or compensating reconciliation against the system-of-record billing platform.

technical_fit.latency_budget: Two regimes. (a) Real-time blocking at the SBC / SMSC / SMS firewall: 10–50 ms per call setup is the operational ceiling so the fraud check fits inside SIP INVITE / MO-SMS forwarding without breaking call-setup KPIs. CPaaS OTP-send paths typically have a 100–500 ms internal budget for the AIT/anti-pumping check before submitting to the operator. Beava's sub-millisecond TCP batch_get fits comfortably. (b) Near-real-time CDR-based investigation and threshold-trigger: seconds to tens of seconds is acceptable, but the industry has moved from hour-batch to sub-minute (Subex ROC FM 8.3 'Online Statistical Rules', Mobileum 'near real-time exchange of records', Neural Technologies '99% within 10 minutes').
technical_fit.feature_freshness_sla: Seconds. IRSF bursts and AIT spikes complete within seconds-to-minutes and the published target is sub-second staleness for the real-time path and <60 s for the analytical path. Beava's push-on-event WAL model gives single-digit-ms feature staleness, which is materially fresher than the hour-batch CDR mediation pipelines most incumbents still run.
technical_fit.throughput_profile: Steady-state EPS varies wildly with carrier size. Order-of-magnitude bounds: a small MVNO sees ~10–50 CDRs/s; a regional CSP (10–30 M subs) sees 1k–10k CDRs/s sustained with 5–20x busy-hour spikes; a large tier-1 operator (>100 M subs) sees 50k–200k CDRs/s sustained and bursts above 1 M/s in busy hour; international wholesale carriers (Sparkle, BICS, iBASIS, Tata Communications, Telia Carrier) and large CPaaS (Twilio, Sinch, Infobip) move tens of billions of minutes / messages annually with sustained tens-of-k EPS and large-bursty peaks. Beava's published 684k EPS sustained on a single Apple-M4 core (TCP+msgpack+parallel=16) sits comfortably above small/mid CSP requirements and inside tier-1 single-node ceilings with margin. [uncertain] specific published CDR-EPS for Subex / Mobileum production tiers; vendors describe 'billions of records per hour' qualitatively rather than committing to a number.
technical_fit.read_to_write_ratio: Write-heavy. Every CDR / EDR / signalling event is one or more writes against multiple entity grains (a-number, b-number, b-prefix, IMSI, cell, trunk); reads happen at decision points (SBC pre-routing, OTP-send pre-submission) and at the fraud-ops dashboard. A reasonable rule of thumb is 1 read per 5–10 writes; AIT or IRSF storms skew it sharply write-heavy.
technical_fit.state_size_estimate: A regional CSP with ~20M active MSISDNs × ~6 entity grains (a-number, b-number, b-prefix, IMSI, IMEI, cell) × ~30–50 features per grain × ~16 bytes per counter ≈ 60–100 GB hot state — inside a single beava box. A global tier-1 with ~300M subscribers plus the international b-prefix fan-out and IMSI-roaming joins pushes into the hundreds of GB to low TB range and would exceed today's single-binary in-memory ceiling. A pure international-wholesale-voice carrier (no retail subs, just prefixes / trunks / peering CDRs) fits very comfortably in single-digit-GB hot state because the cardinality is bounded by E.164 prefix space, not subscriber count.
technical_fit.cardinality_pattern: Mixed. Bounded on b_prefix (E.164 prefix space, ~10^5–10^6 active prefixes worldwide), trunk_id, peer_carrier, app_id, sender_id. Slowly-growing on a_number_hash, msisdn_hash, imsi_hash (subscriber bases grow at single-digit % a year). Explosive on b_number_hash (the called-party population is effectively unbounded because anyone in the world can be called), on (a_number, b_number) pair, and on AIT-driven MSISDN sets (sequential / generated numbers blow out cardinality during an attack). The explosive grains are exactly where HLL / CMS sketches dominate; the bounded prefix grain wants exact counters and small fixed memory.
technical_fit.typical_state_lifecycle_and_ttl: Mixed TTLs. Velocity counters: seconds to days (10s/1m/5m/15m/1h/24h/7d). Per-MSISDN behavioural profile and known-good caller list: 30–90 days. SIM-box detection requires multi-day profiling (a clean SIM looks normal for hours, only the multi-day usage flat-distribution signature exposes it). Subscription-fraud aging: 30–90 days. Interconnect-billing dispute window: 6–12 months (and CDR retention itself is often 6–24 months under national ePrivacy / data-retention rules). Beava's WAL+snapshot fits the seconds-to-90-day hot tier; the multi-month CDR archive belongs in a separate data-lake / lakehouse.
technical_fit.typical_feature_count_per_decision: 20–80+ features per real-time decision. The NDSS-2021 IRSF paper and Subex / Mobileum / Neural Technologies feature lists cite 20–50 engineered features per call; Sinapsio reports 150+ call parameters of which 20+ specifically target flash calls. Beava's batch_get / get-many path is exactly the right shape.
technical_fit.durability_requirements: Crash-safe is the table-stakes minimum: losing the recent velocity counters during a crash creates a multi-second blind spot that AIT / IRSF bursts will immediately exploit, with direct interconnect-settlement P&L impact. Regulator-grade durability is required for the billing-reconciliation and Code-of-Conduct attestation paths; those typically live in a system-of-record DB and beava's role is the hot-path aggregator. Beava's WAL + periodic snapshot + refuse-on-network-FS posture matches the crash-safe tier; for regulator-grade and interconnect-billing-grade, beava needs to be paired with a durable downstream sink (Kafka / Postgres CDC out / S3).
technical_fit.deployment_topology_fit: Single-binary per-region / per-PoP fits the SBC / SMSC sidecar pattern very naturally: a beava box co-located with each SBC or SMSC handles that node's hot CDR / EDR stream with local sub-ms reads. Single-binary-per-tenant fits a CPaaS provider hosting per-customer AIT controls. Multi-region active-active with strong consistency does NOT fit today: beava has no in-process sharding and no cross-region replication in v0, so a global tier-1's centralized fraud platform aggregating CDRs from dozens of switches in dozens of countries cannot use beava as the single source of truth without an external aggregation layer. Hybrid is the realistic v0 topology: beava-at-the-edge for blocking, plus a downstream warehouse for cross-region investigation.

commercial_fit.who_buys: Primarily the fraud-management / revenue-assurance team (Head of Fraud & RA, Director of Wholesale Risk) at MNOs, MVNOs, fixed-line operators, international-voice wholesale carriers and CPaaS providers; the network security / SOC team for signalling-fraud overlap; the wholesale-trading / interconnect team when interconnect-settlement losses are the trigger. Secondary buyers: bypass-detection specialist vendors (Neural Technologies, Heksagon, Mobik, MGCOMM) who could embed beava under their own product.
commercial_fit.market_size_signal: Large, regulator-adjacent, and growing. CFCA's 2023 Global Fraud Loss Survey put global telecom-fraud losses at $38.95B (up 12% YoY, ~2.5% of telecom revenues), with IRSF alone at $6.23B annually and 48% of operators reporting high-volume IRSF attacks (per the GLF 2024 Fraud Report). The telecom-fraud-management software market is variously sized at $5.7–7.6B in 2024–2025 with 10–12% CAGRs and a $16.8B forecast by 2032 (MarketsAndMarkets / Stratistics MRC / Growth Market Reports). AIT / SMS pumping alone was estimated at 19.8–35.7B fraudulent messages and ~$1.15B in OTP-delivery cost in 2023 (Mobilesquared), with X publicly attributing >$60M of losses to SMS pumping in 2022. Incumbent revenue is mostly private but Subex, Mobileum, Neural Technologies, Hiya, LATRO, BICS, NetCracker, Amdocs, Nokia, Ericsson, Tech Mahindra, SAS, FICO, Tata Consultancy Services, IBM and HPE all serve this space. [uncertain] exact private revenue for Subex / Mobileum fraud-product lines.
commercial_fit.urgency_drivers: Five forces: (1) Loss curve — fraud up 12% YoY in 2023; carriers absorb the bill for unsettled IRSF traffic on their interconnect ledgers. (2) Regulation — the GLF / i3Forum Code of Conduct (signed by 22+ international carriers) plus national CDR-retention and ePrivacy rules create audit pressure. (3) Attack velocity — IRSF and AIT now complete in seconds; hour-batch CDR mediation is structurally too slow. (4) CPaaS-customer demand — fintechs and marketplaces directly invoice CPaaS providers for AIT losses (X / Twitter case), and CPaaS providers competitively differentiate on the strength of their AIT controls (Twilio Verify Fraud Guard, Sinch / Vonage / Bandwidth equivalents). (5) 5G + VoLTE + VoWiFi expansion — new bearers add CDR variants the legacy hour-batch pipelines do not yet cover.
commercial_fit.regulatory_or_audit_constraints: GDPR / ePrivacy Directive — CDRs are personal data; retention TTLs, right-to-erasure, and data-residency apply (Italian DPA fined TIM €27.8M in part for excessive CDR retention). National data-retention laws (mandatory CDR retention 6–24 months in many EU states, 12–24 months in many APAC markets) — beava is not the system of record for this archive but must be auditably ephemeral or auditably scoped. GLF / i3Forum Code of Conduct on IRSF — operator-facing, not directly regulatory but audit-relevant. Lawful intercept / LI obligations — strictly a separate path; beava must not be in scope. PCI-DSS — applies when CPaaS routes payment-step verification; beava state should never hold PAN. SOC 2 Type II — table stakes for any CPaaS-vendor buyer. [uncertain] specific national CDR-retention regulations by country.
commercial_fit.time_to_value_signal: A working per-A-number CDR-velocity demo (count of calls and sum of minutes in 1m/5m/1h/24h on a_number_hash with batch_get under 1 ms, plus a b_prefix-match against a hot list) can stand up in roughly 1–2 days on beava given the SDK's @bv.event / @bv.table primitives, especially if seeded with the existing python/beava/demos/fraud/ scaffold. A more realistic 30–50-feature per-A-number / per-B-prefix / per-IMSI / per-cell velocity rig integrated against a real CDR feed (Asterisk / OpenSIPS / Kamailio / Genesys / proprietary SBC) plus a hot-list integration (IPRN test numbers, GLF/i3Forum lists) is typically 2–4 weeks. A production-grade SIM-box detection layer (which needs multi-day behavioural baselines) is 6–12 weeks.

competition.incumbents: Two layers. (a) Generic streaming / feature-store stacks used to build telecom-fraud rigs in-house: Apache Flink (the dominant CDR-streaming choice today — Nussknacker case studies, Confluent / Ververica references), Kafka Streams, Apache Spark Streaming / Real-Time Mode, Redis (still common for hot-counter state), Aerospike (Aerospike has explicit telecom case-study material around billing/charging and fraud), SingleStore (publishes a CDR-fraud vector-functions example), Materialize / RisingWave (SQL streaming substitutes for Flink), Tecton / Feast / Chalk / Hopsworks / Fennel (feature stores layered on top). (b) Stateful primitives inside warehouses (Snowflake Dynamic Tables, Databricks Lakebase) are increasingly used for the analytical tier. Beava competes most directly with the (Redis or Aerospike) + (Flink or Kafka Streams) two-box pattern by collapsing it into a single binary.
competition.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: Domain-specific incumbents that a buyer would otherwise procure as black boxes — and that beava is not directly competing with at the product layer, but rather is the infrastructure they could be built on: Subex (ROC Fraud Management 8.3+), Mobileum (Revenue Share Fraud, SMS Firewall), Neural Technologies (ActivML), Hiya (B2B + CSP, branded calling), LATRO (Fraud Shield), BICS (fraud prevention / SMS firewall), NetCracker (OSS / fraud modules; powers BICS), Symsoft (Sinch division, A2P SMS firewall + fraud), Amdocs, Nokia, Ericsson, Tata Consultancy Services, Tech Mahindra, SAS Institute Fraud Management, FICO, IBM (i2 analytics), HPE, Synaptique, Heksagon, Mobik, MGCOMM, Anam, Enea (Adaptive Mobile / AIT), Openmind Networks, Syniverse, iBASIS, TNS, Sardine (SMS pumping protection), TMT ID, XConnect, TransNexus, AB Handshake. CFCA member surveys and the GLF Code of Conduct provide the meta-coordination layer.
competition.beava_differentiator: Six concrete differentiators for the wholesale-fraud / IRSF / AIT use case: (1) Single binary — no Kafka + Flink + Redis + feature-store ETL chain; collapses three vendors into one box for a fraud team that is not a data-platform team. (2) 50+ first-class aggregation primitives (counters, velocities, distances, distributions) cover exactly the features Subex / Mobileum / Neural Technologies hand-code: per-A-number 1m/5m/1h/24h counts, distinct-B-country fan-out, duration distributions, ratio outbound/inbound. (3) Sub-ms TCP get / batch_get fits inside the SBC / SMSC pre-routing budget with margin, enabling true in-flight blocking rather than hour-batch retrospective detection. (4) Push-on-event ingestion model (HTTP/JSON, framed TCP, msgpack) accepts CDR feeds directly from SBC / SMSC / billing-mediation tap without requiring Kafka in the path — many smaller MVNOs and CPaaS shops do not run Kafka. (5) Apache-2.0 with no open-core split — for a CPaaS provider competing on AIT controls, the licence story matters as much as the throughput. (6) ~684k EPS on one M4 core means beava can sit in a single 1U at PoP-edge alongside the SBC and cover the entire site's CDR fan-out, rather than requiring a regional cluster.
competition.where_beava_loses_today: Concrete gaps blocking production telecom-fraud deployments: (1) No TLS and no auth on :8080/:8081/:8090 — telcos run strict network-segmentation audits; this is an instant non-starter without a sidecar TLS terminator. (2) No in-process sharding — a global tier-1 cannot split a single MSISDN namespace across machines; vertical scaling only. (3) No cross-region replication — multi-region active-active fraud platforms (centralized correlation across roaming partners, international-wholesale interconnects) cannot use beava as the source of truth. (4) In-memory only with refuse-on-network-FS — buyers must accept local NVMe and WAL replay for node loss; interconnect-billing-grade durability needs a downstream sink. (5) No triggers / no 'fire when counter crosses threshold' — fraud teams want 'when a_number_hash exceeds N calls to b_prefix in W seconds, emit BLOCK to the SBC' as a primitive; today the buyer must poll. (6) No multi-tenancy / no namespace ACLs — a CPaaS vendor cannot safely host multiple enterprise customers' AIT controls on one beava box; a wholesale carrier cannot safely host multiple downstream-operator views. (7) No secondary indexes — 'find all A-numbers calling b_prefix X with N>5 in 1m' is not a primary-key get and would need an out-of-band scan; fraud-ops hunter queries depend on this. (8) No native PII / token field marking and no encryption-at-rest — telcos under ePrivacy / national data-retention audit will demand explicit posture. (9) No graph-traversal primitive — IRSF chain unrolling (caller → forwarded-to → forwarded-to → premium) is a graph problem, not a primary-key get. (10) No CDR-format adapters — SBC, SMSC, billing-mediation vendors all emit different CDR / EDR schemas (3GPP TS 32.298 ASN.1, plain CSV, JSON, Avro); v0 expects the user to normalise.
competition.integration_surface: Upstream producers in this domain are heterogeneous and notably not Kafka-only: SBC CDR taps (Oracle ACME, Ribbon, AudioCodes, Sansay, Mavenir, Metaswitch — typically RADIUS-Accounting or syslog or proprietary push), SMSC EDR taps (Mavenir, Ericsson, Nokia, OpenMind, NewNet), billing-mediation outputs (Amdocs, NetCracker, Comarch, MATRIXX, Volt Active Data — emit CDRs to downstream systems at intervals), DPI / signalling probes (Polystar, ELLA Communications, Cisco Joy), 3GPP-standard charging gateways (CGF emitting GTP'-encapsulated CDRs), and CPaaS internal event buses (Twilio / Sinch / Vonage proprietary). The streaming-pipeline shops do typically run Kafka in the middle. Beava's HTTP/JSON :8080 and framed-TCP :8081 (msgpack) map cleanly to the SBC syslog/RADIUS-tap path (with a small adapter) and to the CPaaS internal event bus; a thin Kafka consumer is needed for the streaming-pipeline shops and is not in v0. Downstream consumers are the rules engine (often Drools or vendor-proprietary), the ML scorer (XGBoost / LightGBM / GNN — recent academic work uses graph-based latent-synergy models), and the SOAR / SBC enforcement plane.
competition.scoring_engine_coupling: Both. Hard velocity caps and Code-of-Conduct-aligned rules (e.g., 'no more than N minutes to b_country in T from a fresh subscription') belong in a rules engine. ML scorers (XGBoost / LightGBM / increasingly graph-neural-networks like the latent-synergy-graph approach published in 2023, plus deep learning for SIM-box bypass) consume beava features for the longer-tail signatures. Beava is the feature substrate under both.

adoption_signals.existing_public_users_or_case_studies: No publicly named beava users running telecom-fraud workloads yet. Comparable published case studies that legitimise the shape of the problem: Aerospike telecom AI/ML platform material covering billing/charging + fraud + policy control + subscriber data; Subex ROC Fraud Management 8.3 'Online Statistical Rules' for real-time IRSF detection; Mobileum Revenue Share Fraud with 'near real-time exchange of records'; Neural Technologies ActivML detecting '99% of SIM box activity within 10 minutes'; Ethio-Telecom SIM-box detection deep-learning case study; Cameroon fixed/mobile operator SIM-box bypass CDR ML case study; the NDSS-2021 IRSF paper validating 98% accuracy / 0.28% FPR on real European-operator CDRs; SingleStore CDR-fraud vector-functions demo; Nussknacker (Flink) Plus-Telecom CDR streaming-fraud case study; Sardine SMS pumping protection deployed at fintech / marketplace customers.
adoption_signals.community_discussions: [uncertain] No specific beava Discord / GitHub Discussion threads on telecom CDR fraud identified in this research pass. Broader community signals are strong: CFCA member-only discussion forums, GLF / i3Forum communiques, Commsrisk blog, Capacity Media, TheFastMode, abhandshake.com (AB Handshake) blog all run continuous telco-fraud discourse. Hacker News thread 'Twilio's toll fraud problem' (id 34265433) is a high-visibility public discussion.
adoption_signals.examples_or_demos_in_repo: No telecom-specific demo in the repo yet. The existing `python/beava/demos/fraud/` directory contains an e-commerce/payment-flavoured `schema.json` + `events.jsonl` (event name 'Txn'), and `crates/beava-bench/configs/fraud-team.json` is the same payment-flavoured benchmark. A dedicated `python/beava/demos/telecom_cdr/` with voice_cdr / sms_edr / signalling_event shapes plus a per-A-number / per-B-prefix velocity wiring is a clear gap. [uncertain] whether the existing `geo.json` bench config is intended for telecom.
adoption_signals.adversarial_pressure_level: High / active adversary. Telecom wholesale fraud is one of the oldest organised-crime-adjacent fraud verticals: IRSF rings rotate A-numbers and B-prefixes within hours, SIM-box operators rotate IMSIs and IMEIs, AIT operators generate new MSISDN ranges and time their bursts around CPaaS rate-limit windows, Wangiri operators iterate target lists daily. Feature drift, label drift, and concept drift are all aggressive.

risk_and_non_goals.non_goals: Beava is the wrong tool for: (1) Long historical lookbacks (90+ day per-MSISDN behavioural profiles for ML training — warehouse / lakehouse / offline feature store). (2) Full CDR archive for national-data-retention compliance (6–24 months mandated retention belongs in a regulated archive, not an in-memory aggregator). (3) Cross-entity graph traversal for IRSF chain unrolling and call-forwarding-loop detection — beava is keyed by primary entity, not a graph query engine; Neo4j / TigerGraph / Memgraph fit better here. (4) Batch model training and backfill (offline feature generation belongs in Spark / Snowflake / Databricks). (5) Lawful intercept (LI) — strictly separate path. (6) Billing system of record — beava is the hot-path aggregator, not the billable-CDR archive. (7) Cross-operator interconnect-settlement reconciliation requiring strong consistency across continents (beava has no cross-region replication).
risk_and_non_goals.open_engineering_gaps: Concrete features beava would need to ship to be production-grade for telecom-fraud at a mid-to-large CSP / wholesale carrier / CPaaS: (1) TLS on all three listeners (:8080, :8081, :8090) plus mTLS option — table stakes for any telco network audit. (2) AuthN/AuthZ — API-key auth scoped per namespace at minimum, ideally JWT/OIDC; per-topic and per-entity-grain ACLs to support multi-tenant CPaaS hosting. (3) Triggers / event-driven actions — 'when a_number_hash crosses threshold T in window W, emit BLOCK action to a webhook / SBC SIP-redirect / Kafka topic' is the single highest-impact missing primitive for this domain. (4) Multi-tenancy with hard namespace isolation, per-tenant quotas, per-tenant auth (so a wholesale carrier can host multiple downstream-operator views, or a CPaaS can host per-customer AIT controls). (5) In-process sharding and consistent-hashing for entities so vertical limits do not cap a global tier-1. (6) Cross-region replication (active-active or active-passive with bounded staleness) for multi-PoP fraud platforms. (7) Approximate-aggregate primitives as first-class: HLL n_unique for distinct-B-number fan-out, CMS top-K for top-offender prefixes / IPs, t-digest for duration distributions. (8) Secondary indexes or scan APIs for fraud-ops hunter queries ('find top-N A-numbers by sum(billed_minutes) to b_country=X in last 10m'). (9) Configurable per-feature TTLs and eviction so 90-day per-MSISDN profiles can coexist with 10-second velocity counters. (10) Explicit PII / token-field marking, encryption-at-rest, and audit log for ePrivacy / national-data-retention / SOC 2 audits. (11) CDR-format adapters: 3GPP TS 32.298 ASN.1 BER, RADIUS-Accounting, SBC syslog, CDR-on-Demand REST, GTP' CGF, and the major billing-mediation outputs (Amdocs / NetCracker / MATRIXX / Volt). (12) Hot-list ingest helper for GLF / i3Forum / IPRN test-number lists with daily refresh and atomic swap. (13) Graph-edge co-storage or a 'lookup neighbour entity' primitive for chain-unrolling without needing a separate Neo4j. (14) Durable downstream sink (Kafka / Postgres CDC out / S3) for interconnect-billing reconciliation.
risk_and_non_goals.trigger_action_required: Yes, strongly. Telecom-fraud is one of the strongest pulls for the trigger/action gap: the difference between 'detect IRSF in 60 s' and 'detect IRSF after 0.5 billed minutes' is real currency on the interconnect-settlement ledger. Fraud teams want 'when counter crosses threshold, fire SIP-redirect / SMSC-drop / API-key-throttle' as a primitive, not 'poll every N ms'. Today beava cannot do this natively, which is the single largest functional gap for the domain.
